title: Monte Carlo Poker Equity Simulator
summary: My MITES Semester project uses repeated deals to estimate Texas Hold’em equity from known cards.
question: How much of the pot is a hand worth when some of the cards are still unknown?

sections.title: What I built
sections.text: The simulator samples unseen cards, finds each player’s best five-card hand, and compares the ranks with exact tie-break rules. A fixed random seed lets a scenario be rerun. I separated the Python simulation from the Streamlit interface.

sections.title: What I learned
sections.text: Equity includes the share of the pot you take when a hand ties. Making that distinction meant testing split pots as well as edge cases in hand ranking, from ace-low straights to kicker ties.
